title: Define non-functional requirements such as SLAs, RTO (Recovery Time Objective) and RPO (Recovery Point Objective)
description: Before going to production, it is very important to decide the target of availability and recovery time you are looking for. This will help you to decide the right backup strategy but also the architecture of your solution.

title: Rehearse recovery into a clean, isolated environment
description: Regularly rebuild the platform from infrastructure as code in an isolated recovery environment. Restore application configuration and data, measure RTO/RPO, and test dependencies and access. Never delete production merely to conduct a recovery rehearsal.

documentation.title: Rehearse recovery into a clean, isolated environment

title: Distribute production workloads across availability zones
description: Use supported zonal node pools and topology spread constraints to separate replicas across nodes and zones. Validate sufficient surviving capacity, zonal storage behavior, load balancing, and failure recovery; availability zones are separate datacenter failure domains within a region.

documentation.title: Distribute production workloads across availability zones

title: Design multiregion recovery around business requirements
description: Choose active-active or active-passive regions based on RTO/RPO, data residency, latency, dependencies, and available capacity. Regions need not be an Azure region pair; validate service support, replication, quota, and independence explicitly.

documentation.title: Design multiregion recovery around business requirements

title: Test global traffic failover and failback
description: Select Front Door or Traffic Manager according to protocol and routing needs. Test health probes, DNS caching, TLS, session behavior, regional dependencies, and failback. Routing changes do not recover or synchronize application data.

documentation.title: Test global traffic failover and failback

title: Create a storage migration plan
description: Your applications might use Azure Storage for their data. Because your applications are spread across multiple AKS clusters in different regions, you need to keep the storage synchronized

documentation.title: Backup, restore and migrate Kubernetes resources including state to another AKS cluster with Velero

title: Select an AKS tier with the required control-plane SLA
description: Use Standard or Premium tier for the financially backed Kubernetes API-server uptime SLA. Microsoft documents 99.95% with availability zones and 99.9% without; Free tier has no financially backed SLA. These are control-plane commitments, not an end-to-end application SLA; verify current contractual terms.

documentation.title: Select an AKS tier with the required control-plane SLA

title: Spread replicas across nodes and zones
description: Use topology spread constraints or appropriate anti-affinity to keep replicas in separate failure domains. Balance strict scheduling rules against available recovery capacity, and test both node loss and zone loss under representative load.

documentation.title: Spread replicas across nodes and zones

title: If using a private registry (ACR), configure region replication to store images in multiple regions
description: Companies that want a local presence, or a hot backup, choose to run services from multiple Azure regions.
detail: As a best practice, placing a container registry in each region where images are run allows network-close operations, enabling fast, reliable image layer transfers. Geo-replication enables an Azure container registry to function as a single registry, serving multiple regions with multi-master regional registries.

title: Configure your registry to use zone redundancy
description: Use Azure availability zones to create a resilient and high availability Azure container registry within an Azure region.

documentation.title: Enable zone redundancy in Azure Container Registry for resiliency and high availability

title: Move Container Registry to a dedicated resource group
description: Because container registries are resources that are used across multiple container hosts, a registry should reside in its own resource group.
detail: Although you might experiment with a specific host type, such as Azure Container Instances, you’ll likely want to delete the container instance when you’re done. However, you might also want to keep the collection of images you pushed to Azure Container Registry. By placing your registry in its own resource group, you minimize the risk of accidentally deleting the collection of images in the registry when you delete the container instance resource group.

documentation.title: Registry best practices - Use dedicated resource group

title: Evaluate ACR soft delete against support and retention requirements
description: Where supported, evaluate ACR soft delete to recover accidentally deleted artifacts within the configured retention period. Check current feature status, limitations, and costs; soft delete does not replace immutable release retention, replication, or tested disaster recovery.

title: Back up supported cluster resources and persistent volumes
description: Configure Azure Backup for AKS or a supported alternative with explicit scope, retention, and recovery objectives. Check the current support matrix for Azure Disk/Azure Files, snapshot versus vaulted backup, regions, and cross-region restore. Back up external databases separately.

documentation.title: Back up supported cluster resources and persistent volumes

detail: Perform full restore drills, including identities, CRDs, secrets, application dependencies, and data consistency. A successful backup job does not prove that the application can be recovered.

title: Exercise failure scenarios under representative load
description: Rehearse pod, node, zone, DNS, registry, egress, and dependency failures in a controlled environment. Use fault injection only with explicit scope and safety controls, verify service objectives, and track remediation actions from each exercise.

documentation.title: Exercise failure scenarios under representative load
